title_pattern: Hashtag-only caption (#edit #anime #animetkitok #animerecommendation), no story text at all. The hashtags are discovery bait for the anime-edit audience, not a description; the real 'title' is the burned-in first caption 'rules for nightshift truckers'. Pattern: zero-information caption + the hook lives entirely inside the video. Looks like a translated repost of a Chinese animated horror series (per BRIEF rule 5: study structure only).

thumbnail.composition: TikTok default cover = first frame. 9:16 canvas, black top and bottom bars, a 16:9 picture band in the middle: anime-style painted night landscape of a serpentine mountain road through dark forest, glowing crescent moon top right, a white box truck small in the lower left foreground. One line of caption sits in the black bar just above the picture.
thumbnail.text: 'rules for nightshift truckers' in white italic lowercase sans, ~4% of frame height, no punctuation, centered above the image band
thumbnail.colours: Deep navy/indigo and violet night palette, cool blue-white highlights on the road and moon, black letterbox; the white truck and white text are the only bright neutrals
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Tiny lone truck vs a huge empty winding mountain road under the moon: isolation and vulnerability. No faces on the cover.
thumbnail.why_it_works: 'Rules for X' is a proven horror framing (implies breaking a rule = danger) and is readable at thumbnail size; the lonely road at night sets genre and mood instantly. The letterbox + caption-in-bar look signals 'story series' to people who have watched this format before. Weak as a standalone thumbnail; the video wins on in-feed autoplay and retention, not on cover clicks.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: You know the unspoken rules for night shift truckers? Don't gawk at accident scenes and never pull over for hitchhikers at midnight.
hook.verbatim_0_11s: You know the unspoken rules for night shift truckers? Don't gawk at accident scenes and never pull over for hitchhikers at midnight. Don't think just because you're driving a big rig you're immune to trouble. My mentor drilled these rules into me for over a decade. But tonight I broke them.
hook.device: Rhetorical-question cold open into a 'rules list' (three rules in 7s), backed by a mentor's authority, then an instant rule-break ('But tonight I broke them' at ~9-11s) that sets up dread: the viewer knows which rule is about to be broken (pulling over at midnight) and the story delivers it at 11s. Visuals cut every ~2s: establishing night road -> burning crash -> narrator in cab.

beats.summary: Question hook: unspoken rules for night truckers; three rules (no gawking at crashes, no midnight hitchhikers, a big rig won't save you), from a mentor of ten years.
'But tonight I broke them.' Explicit open loop that the rest is consequence.
Midnight: family of four flags him down; father kowtows; black sedan stalled on the shoulder; all terrified; he lets them in.
Father says a strange red sports car chased them down the mountain road; narrator brushes it off (big truck, nobody messes with me) - false safety.
Radio reports a crash on this very road: red sports car vs black sedan, red-car driver died. Narrator kills the radio before it finishes (withheld info).
Father pales: 'the car chasing us was red too'. Family stares at each other. Narrator rationalises: crash was three years ago, radio flashback. Tension parked, not released.
Cigarette, names exchanged (Old Mo, wife Luo Ying, kids), smiles in the mirror, 'picking up our daughter', 'hitting a temple to pray' - humanising lull that plants more oddities.
The 'little girl' is about twenty; in college but it's not a holiday - wife freezes. Unanswered question.
Son's dry, deep, raspy cough; father harshly orders him to hold it in instead of comforting him; father's awkward smile. Each detail hints the family is not what they seem.
Engine roar from behind: 'It's that red sports car again!' Headlights, red blur charging; family huddles, father clutches head.
Rearview mirror: convertible driver's head hanging out over the windshield, mouth wide open, screaming. Narrator misreads it as a street racer.
Single-lane mountain road, endless horn, driver tries to squeeze between truck and cliff; narrator won't yield; 'grim reaper swinging his scythe'; father muttering nonstop.

Narrator swerves round the bend; red car forced back, sparks, skid marks. Video ends mid-scene with no resolution (implied part 2) - the reader suspects the family are the ghosts and the red-car driver was trying to warn him.

pacing.note_wpm: Very fast narration (~281 wpm) - TTS clearly sped up ~1.4-1.6x; captions change every ~1.6 s (105 cues).
pacing.note_shots: Distinct compositions every ~2-6 s (median ~3 s); ffmpeg scene detection found only 3 hard cuts because shots are cross-dissolves/same palette and many 'shots' are the same background with swapped character poses. Re-hook every ~10-15 s via a new anomaly or threat.
pacing.caption_style: One line, 6-9 words, white italic lowercase sans, no punctuation, in the black bar above the 16:9 image band, synced to TTS chunks
pacing.music_sfx: Not analysed from audio waveform here; radio/engine/horn moments are marked visually with red tick 'noise' lines

transcript_source: TikTok auto-subs (eng-US) downloaded with yt-dlp; matches burned-in captions
techniques_worth_copying: 'Rules for <job>' cold open: question + 3 rules in 7 s + mentor authority + 'but tonight I broke them' by 10 s.
Break the most specific rule within 2 s of stating the break (pull over at midnight -> family flagging at 11 s).
Radio/news report as an ominous clue that the narrator cuts off before it finishes - withheld information the viewer completes themselves.
False rationalisation ('it was a crash three years ago, just a flashback') parks tension instead of releasing it.
Domestic lull (names, cigarette, smiles) seeded with small wrong details (adult 'little girl', not a holiday, forbidden cough, bruise smudges) - each one a micro re-hook.
Reversal-ready setup: the 'threat' (red car) is probably the warning and the 'victims' are the ghosts; the viewer can sense it before the narrator does (dramatic irony drives comments).
End mid-action with no resolution -> part-2 follow / rewatch / comment bait.
Letterboxed 16:9 image band in a 9:16 frame with caption in the top bar: cheap, consistent, readable.

Cheap cartoon characters (round white heads, mop hair, simple mouths) composited on moody semi-realistic painted backgrounds; reuse the same 4-5 backgrounds (cab side, cab interior wide, windshield POV, road exterior, aerial road) for the whole episode.
Red tick-mark 'noise' lines to visualise sound (radio, engine roar, horn) without SFX graphics.
code_only_remake_needs: Layout: 1080x1920 canvas, black, centred 16:9 band (1080x608) at y~560; caption line in the top bar at y~460, white italic lowercase sans ~44px, one TTS chunk at a time.

Character rig in SVG: round white head, mop-hair path (2-3 hair variants + colours), dot eyes, eyebrow angle, 5-6 mouth shapes for flap/lip-sync, body as a coloured rounded rectangle; expressions: neutral, scared (sweat drop, raised brows), smile, frown; hands-on-head pose; face smudge overlay (grey-green/purple blur) for 'wrong' characters.

Backgrounds as layered SVG/Canvas paintings with gradients and blur: truck cab side window with night trees, cab interior wide (back seat), windshield POV with dashboard, radio close-up with animated waveform LCD, rearview mirror, night forest road (one-point perspective), aerial serpentine road with moving truck, crashed cars (simplified vector cars), moon/stars sky. Cool navy/teal palette with fog gradients and vignette.
Vehicles: vector truck (side, front, top-down) and sports car (front with bloom headlights, top-down with tail-light streaks); headlight bloom via radial gradients + SVG blur filter.

Camera: slow Ken Burns push-in on every shot (scale 1.0->1.08), occasional punch-in for close-ups, aerial path-follow animation for the truck along an SVG path (getPointAtLength), crossfade transitions (~0.3 s) and one fast whip-blur.
Sound-visual cues: red tick-mark burst sprite near sources (radio, engine, horn), screen shake on the swerve, spark particles + skid-mark stroke-dashoffset reveal.
Audio: Kokoro TTS narrator at ~1.4x speed (target 250-280 wpm), distinct pitch for dialogue lines optional; low drone + engine/horn SFX from a CC0 library or synthesized.
Storyboard schema: per caption chunk -> background id, characters with pose/expression, camera move, transition, sfx cue; ~40 shots for 166 s.
